quote: New § 14.4 permits Supplier to assign the Agreement, in whole or in part, without Customer's consent to (a) any Affiliate of Supplier or (b) any successor by merger, consolidation, change of control, or sale of substantially all assets... Harrowgate could find itself in an exclusive, multi-year supply relationship with an unknown entity — a newly acquired subsidiary, a financial-sponsor-owned successor, or a competitor's affiliate — with no right to object or terminate.
reason: The memo correctly identifies new § 14.4 in Amendment No. 1, which lets Veltmar assign without consent to Affiliates or successors. It also says in passing that the assignee could be a competitor's affiliate. It fails the criterion's other required element: it never says Harrowgate is still bound by the § 14.3 consent requirement, so it does not show the restriction is now one-sided. It also does not analyze § 14.4 as overriding § 14.3. The only trace of that is the 'Notwithstanding Section 14.3' wording in the proposed redraft, and that redraft adds no competitor exclusion. Under a strict reading the issue is only partly identified.
